proofs.proof_tex:
Fix the known point \(x_0\in[0,1]^d\), and abbreviate
\[
 \mathcal P=\mathcal P(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L),\qquad
 r_P(T)=\mathbb E_{P_O^{\otimes n}}
 \left|T(O_{1:n})-\tau_P(x_0)\right|.
\]
The estimator \(\widehat\tau_n(x_0)\) in
\(\mathrm{def:total\mbox{-}estimator}\) is a Borel function of the data on
both its nonsingular and fallback branches.  Hence the definition of \(R_n\)
and \(\mathrm{lem:closed\mbox{-}regime\mbox{-}fixed\mbox{-}point\mbox{-}upper}\)
give, uniformly in \(x_0\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 R_n
 &=\inf_{T\ \mathrm{Borel}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}r_P(T)\\
 &\le \sup_{P\in\mathcal P}r_P\!\left(\widehat\tau_n(x_0)\right)
 \le C_0\rho_n .                                                   \tag{1}
 \end{aligned}
\]
This is a minimax upper bound witnessed by one data-only estimator, rather
than by a law-dependent oracle family.

For the converse, invoke
\(\mathrm{lem:closed\mbox{-}regime\mbox{-}fixed\mbox{-}point\mbox{-}component\mbox{-}mixtures}\).
It supplies finite priors \(\Pi_+\) and \(\Pi_-\), both supported on the same
class \(\mathcal P\), such that \(\tau_P(x_0)=\theta_\varepsilon\) for every
\(P\) in the support of \(\Pi_\varepsilon\), where
\[
 \Delta:=|\theta_+-\theta_-|\ge c_0\rho_n,                          \tag{2}
\]
and such that the genuine fixed-\(n\) product mixtures
\[
 \mathsf M_\varepsilon
 :=\int P_O^{\otimes n}\,d\Pi_\varepsilon(P),\qquad
 \varepsilon\in\{+,-\},                                           \tag{3}
\]
satisfy \(H^2(\mathsf M_+,\mathsf M_-)\le1/4\).  In particular, no
Poissonized experiment or conditional occupancy event occurs in (3).

Let \(\lambda=\mathsf M_++\mathsf M_-\), and write
\(m_+=d\mathsf M_+/d\lambda\) and
\(m_-=d\mathsf M_-/d\lambda\).  By Cauchy--Schwarz and then the fact that
both densities integrate to one,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \|\mathsf M_+-\mathsf M_-\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 &=\frac12\int|\sqrt{m_+}-\sqrt{m_-}|
                  (\sqrt{m_+}+\sqrt{m_-})\,d\lambda\\
 &\le \frac12 H(\mathsf M_+,\mathsf M_-)
 \left\{\int(\sqrt{m_+}+\sqrt{m_-})^2\,d\lambda\right\}^{1/2}\\
 &\le H(\mathsf M_+,\mathsf M_-)
 \le\frac12 .                                                       \tag{4}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Indeed, the integral in braces is at most four because
\(\int\sqrt{m_+m_-}\,d\lambda\le1\).

Now fix an arbitrary Borel estimator \(T\).  Define the Borel test
\(\varphi\in\{+,-\}\) to select whichever of \(\theta_+\) and
\(\theta_-\) is nearer to \(T\), breaking ties deterministically.  The
triangle inequality shows that
\[
 \{\varphi=-\}\subseteq
 \{|T-\theta_+|\ge\Delta/2\},\qquad
 \{\varphi=+\}\subseteq
 \{|T-\theta_-|\ge\Delta/2\}.                                     \tag{5}
\]
Since the supremum of a nonnegative function over \(\mathcal P\) dominates
its average under either prior, (2)--(5) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P}r_P(T)
 &\ge \frac12\sum_{\varepsilon\in\{+,-\}}
       \int r_P(T)\,d\Pi_\varepsilon(P)\\
 &\ge \frac{\Delta}{4}
       \{\mathsf M_+(\varphi=-)+\mathsf M_-(\varphi=+)\}\\
 &\ge \frac{\Delta}{4}
       \{1-\|\mathsf M_+-\mathsf M_-\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\}\\
 &\ge \frac{c_0}{8}\rho_n .                                      \tag{6}
 \end{aligned}
\]
For the third line, with \(B=\{\varphi=+\}\), the expression in braces on
the preceding line equals
\(1-\{\mathsf M_+(B)-\mathsf M_-(B)\}\), which is at least one minus the
total variation distance.  Taking the infimum of (6) over all Borel \(T\),
combining with (1), and setting \(c=\min\{c_0/8,C_0\}\) and \(C=C_0\)
proves
\[
 c\rho_n\le R_n\le C\rho_n,
 \qquad
 \rho_n=n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta)))}                 \tag{7}
\]
for every \(n\ge2\), with positive finite constants depending only on the
fixed tuple \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) and uniform in \(x_0\).

The support assertion in the component-mixture lemma says that every law
averaged in (3) has exact uniform covariate design, bounded propensity,
interior Bernoulli regressions, the stipulated H\"older regularity, and the
causal completion required by \(\mathrm{def:exact\mbox{-}model}\).  Thus (6)
is a lower bound in the stated fixed-\(n\) i.i.d. experiment.  If a broader
model contains \(\mathcal P\) and uses the same point target, then for every
\(T\) its supremum risk over the broader model is no smaller than its
supremum risk over \(\mathcal P\); taking infima transfers the lower bound in
(7) to that broader model.  Equation (1), by contrast, has only been supplied
on \(\mathcal P\), so it yields no upper bound on the broader model.

Finally, at \(S=S_\star=d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\),
\[
 \eta
 =\left(1+\frac d{2\gamma}+\frac d{2S_\star}\right)^{-1}
 =\left(1+\frac d{2\gamma}+\frac{2\gamma+d}{2\gamma}\right)^{-1}
 =\frac\gamma{2\gamma+d}.                                         \tag{8}
\]
Therefore (7) is exactly the oracle power
\(n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\), with no logarithmic multiplier.  If
\(S<S_\star\), then \(d/(2S)>d/(2S_\star)\), so
\(\eta<\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), and (7) gives
\[
 \frac{R_n}{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}}
 \asymp n^{\gamma/(2\gamma+d)-\eta}\longrightarrow\infty .        \tag{9}
\]
Thus, within the stipulated closed at-or-below-elbow regime, the same-class
oracle benchmark is attained exactly at the elbow.

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives a lower bound on a broader bounded-density pointwise CATE class, while Theorem 2 gives an upper bound under additional design and nuisance-estimation conditions; the displayed lower hard laws use separated local support.
Theorem 2.1 bounds the affinity of two convex mixtures of product measures under a measurable partition and coordinate-local perturbations.
Theorems 3--5 establish matched local and global conditional-variance rates under random design using local U-statistics and coupled lower laws.
Theorem 3 and Corollary 4 give local-polynomial R-learner upper rates with deterministic smoothness-dependent tuning under known-density conditions.
The paper proves a quasi-oracle error bound for an R-learner under sufficient nuisance accuracy rather than a rough-nuisance pointwise minimax converse.

prose_updates.related_work: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE is the closest comparator: its lower theorem covers a broader bounded-density class and its upper theorem requires additional design and nuisance-estimation conditions, whereas the present result closes the fixed-sample-size converse and matching upper bound on the strict exact-uniform bounded-overlap Bernoulli/interiority subclass. The lower converse therefore transfers upward by subclass inclusion to any broader model that contains this subclass and uses the same point target; the exact-uniform upper proof does not transfer in that direction and is not claimed there. RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009SemiparametricMinimax supplies the product-mixture perspective, but the shared smooth frames here require random overlap-component factorization rather than a deterministic coordinate-local partition. ShenGaoWittenHan2020Variance is a random-design nonlinear-functional analogue for repeated local occupancy. Kennedy2023DRCATE and NieWager2021RLearner provide oracle-facing upper comparisons, while RobinsLiTchetgenVanderVaart2008HOIF motivates the finite projection correction. WagerAthey2018CausalForests is an application-facing consumer: this is a precision benchmark for causal-forest and R-learner workflows, not a claim that existing forests attain the bound. LiuMukherjeeRobinsTchetgen2021Adaptive studies adaptive nonlinear-functional estimation, whereas the present estimator uses the known smoothness tuple for deterministic tuning. LeeOkuiWhang2017CATEBands studies uniform CATE confidence bands, whereas this note proves pointwise mean-absolute risk only and supplies no coverage theorem. AtheyWager2021PolicyLearning studies policy-value and regret learning rather than pointwise CATE minimax precision. ChernozhukovWuthrichZhu2021Conformal studies conformal counterfactual and synthetic-control inference rather than this pointwise CATE estimand or its minimax mean-risk guarantee.
